title: Evaluation at a final indexing object detects coherent colimit cocones
statement: Use quasicategories, coherent functors, functor simplicial sets, constant diagrams, equivalence edges and right-pinched mapping spaces of [def-cbc-enhanced-diagrams-cones]. Work in a fixed sufficiently large universe. Let $J$ and $\mathcal C$ be quasicategories, let $t\in J$ be final, meaning that $\operatorname{Map}_J(j,t)$ is contractible for every vertex $j$, and let $d:J\to\mathcal C$ be a coherent functor. For every vertex $w\in\mathcal C$, evaluation at $t$ induces a weak homotopy equivalence of spaces $$\operatorname{ev}_t:\operatorname{Map}_{\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal C)}(d,\Delta_Jw)\longrightarrow\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(d(t),w).$$ For every vertex $l\in\mathcal C$ and coherent cocone $\mu:d\to\Delta_Jl$, the cocone $\mu$ is colimiting if and only if its component $\mu_t:d(t)\to l$ is an equivalence edge. No other colimits in $\mathcal C$ are assumed; the equivalence concerns the entire spaces of coherent cocones, including all higher homotopies.

source.place: Corollary 7.2.2.5 (02XV), absolute colimit specialization of the final-object clause, and Example 7.2.1.4 (03LQ), inclusion of a final object is right cofinal. These are Kerodon tags, not Stacks tags. The coherent cocone formulation uses the mapping-space universal property, equivalently the identity-leg colimit in lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit. Read online 2026-10-17; archival copy WANTED. The web rendering of the second clause of 02XV displays a left cone although the colimit assertion uses a right cone; the dual clause and its restriction to {t}^triangleright give the intended right-cone assertion.

proof.text: Put $a=d(t)$, $D=\operatorname{Fun}(J,\mathcal C)$ and $B(w)=\operatorname{Map}_D(d,\Delta_Jw)$. All the simplicial sets fit in the stipulated containing universe; choose the space universe to contain their mapping simplicial sets. The functor-category and Kan assertions of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] apply with shape $J$, so $D$ is a quasicategory and the mapping spaces in question are Kan. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-final-index-colimit] to the given $J,t,d$. Its finality hypothesis is exactly the assumed contractibility of $\operatorname{Map}_J(j,t)$. It supplies a cocone $\alpha:d\to\Delta_Ja$ with $\alpha_t=\operatorname{id}_a$, such that for every $w$ the induced map $c_w:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(a,w)\to B(w)$, $u\mapsto\Delta_J(u)\circ\alpha$, is a weak homotopy equivalence. This is the mapping-space universal property expressly included in that node's statement, with no assumption of any other colimits.

source.place: Example 7.2.1.4 (03LQ), with the colimit dual of Corollary 7.2.2.11 (02XU); use the existing identity-leg mapping-space colimit statement.

proof.text:
Let $r_w:B(w)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(a,w)$ be restriction to $t$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality] to the simplicial evaluation functor $D\to\mathcal C$ and the constant-diagram functor $\mathcal C\to D$. Its induced maps are the actual right-pinched maps and preserve composition and identity classes on entire mapping spaces. Evaluation of a constant diagram or constant transformation is the original object or transformation, in every simplicial degree. Therefore
$$r_wc_w(u)\simeq u\circ\alpha_t=u\circ\operatorname{id}_a\simeq u.$$
These are homotopies of maps of spaces, not just equations on components. Since $c_w$ is a weak equivalence by Step 1 and $r_wc_w$ is homotopic to the identity, $r_w$ is a weak equivalence. Explicitly on components its map is the inverse of that of $c_w$; on every based homotopy group the same equation makes its induced homomorphism inverse to that of $c_w$, after the basepoint identifications supplied by the homotopy. This proves the first assertion, including all higher homotopy groups.

source.place: Corollary 8.3.5.8 (046J) and Remark 8.3.5.9 (03PD); agent two-out-of-three argument using the identity leg.

proof.text:
Fix a specified cocone $\mu:d\to\Delta_Jl$ and put $f=\mu_t:a\to l$. The dual cocone assertion of [lem-cbc-enhanced-functor-cone-calculus] says that $\mu$ is initial in the coherent cocone category, hence colimiting by the coherent cocone definition, exactly when
$$q_w:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(l,w)\longrightarrow B(w),\qquad u\longmapsto\Delta_J(u)\circ\mu$$
is a weak equivalence for every $w$. In particular this is the criterion for the specified cocone, not only for the chosen $\alpha$. Apply [lem-coef-infinity-hom-bifunctor-functoriality] to evaluation again. It gives the homotopy of entire mapping-space maps
$$r_wq_w\simeq f^*,\qquad f^*(u)=u\circ f.$$
As $r_w$ is a weak equivalence by Step 2, the induced maps on components and based homotopy groups show that $q_w$ is a weak equivalence if and only if $f^*$ is. Thus $\mu$ is colimiting exactly when every precomposition map $f^*:\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(l,w)\to\operatorname{Map}_{\mathcal C}(a,w)$ is a weak equivalence.

source.place: Corollary 7.2.2.5 (02XV), absolute colimit clause; agent expansion using the existing coherent comma cocone criterion and Hom-functor naturality.

proof.text: Suppose $f$ is an equivalence edge. Its inverse data gives an edge $g:l\to a$ with $[g][f]=[\operatorname{id}_a]$ and $[f][g]=[\operatorname{id}_l]$. By the associative and unital composition homotopies and the dependence of precomposition only on the edge's component class in [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition], precomposition by $g$ is a homotopy inverse to precomposition by $f$: for $v:l\to w$ and $u:a\to w$ the two composites are homotopic to $v\circ(f\circ g)\simeq v$ and $u\circ(g\circ f)\simeq u$, respectively. Consequently $f^*$ is a weak equivalence for every $w$, since homotopy inverse maps induce inverse maps on components and all homotopy groups. Step 3 proves that $\mu$ is colimiting.

source.place: Subsection 4.6.8: Propositions 4.6.8.11 and 4.6.8.12 and Notation 4.6.8.15; precomposition by an equivalence has an inverse.

proof.text:
Conversely suppose $\mu:d\to\Delta_Jl$ is colimiting, and write $a=d(t)$ and $f=\mu_t:a\to l$. Step 3 makes $f^*$ a bijection on components for every $w$. With $w=a$, surjectivity supplies a component represented by an edge $g:l\to a$ such that $[g][f]=[\operatorname{id}_a]$. The edge representative and the ordinary category law on components are supplied by [lem-coef-infinity-mapping-composition]. With $w=l$, injectivity of $f^*$ and
$$([f][g])[f]=[f]([g][f])=[f]=[\operatorname{id}_l][f]$$
give $[f][g]=[\operatorname{id}_l]$. Hence $[f]$ is invertible in $h\mathcal C$. The same cited node states precisely that an edge whose component class is invertible admits an inverse edge with both inverse-triangle $2$-simplices. By definition, an edge in a quasicategory is an equivalence edge exactly when such an inverse edge and the two inverse-triangle $2$-simplices exist. Therefore $\mu_t=f$ is an equivalence edge. This proves the other direction without invoking a Yoneda theorem or assuming any further colimits.

source.place: Subsection 4.6.8, Remark 4.6.8.14 and Notation 4.6.8.15; Definition 1.4.6.1 and Remarks 1.4.6.6 and 1.4.6.8 for equivalence edges. Agent two-test-object inverse argument.

lean.statement: theorem final_index_cocone_criterion {J C : SSet.{u}} [Quasicategory J] [Quasicategory C] (t : J _⦋0⦌) (ht : IsTerminal J t) (d : J ⟶ C) : (∀ w : C _⦋0⦌, IsWeakHomotopyEquivalence (finalIndexEvaluationMap t d w)) ∧ (∀ l : C _⦋0⦌, ∀ (μ : (coconeCategory d) _⦋0⦌), μ.1.1 = l → (IsColimiting d μ ↔ IsEquivalenceEdge C (finalIndexCoconeComponent d μ t)))
lean.note: The helper maps evaluation to the literal diagram value and extracts the specified cocone component; both use the canonical constructions of EnhancedDiagramsCones. The theorem states the weak-equivalence and equivalence-edge criteria exactly.
